cases.evidence_note: p970 p. 16, Example 5, entire scholarship included: "The qualified education expenses would be $6,000, and the AGI and MAGI would be $29,625. The tax liability before any credits would be $603. Jane would be able to receive a $1,603 American opportunity credit ($1,000 refundable and $603 nonrefundable), a $1,700 additional child tax credit, and a $3,325 EIC. In total, Jane would be able to receive a tax refund of $6,025." Class A covers lines 11b, 16, 8, 19, 29, 28, 27a and 33/34; line 27 is the $4,000 cap of the stated $6,000 and line 7 $2,500 follows. Schedule 1 line 8r $5,500, worksheet line 2a $0. The EIC at $3,325 requires the line 8r scholarship to be outside earned income (AGI phase-out). Jane is 28, unmarried, files head of household with her 10-year-old qualifying child (EIC and child tax credit), first-year full-time certificate student; wages $24,125 on a W-2 with no withholding and no other income or adjustments, except the scholarship she includes in income, entered on Schedule 1 line 8r. "Jane and the college meet all the requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No, line 26 No; born before 2002, so the line 7 refundability test does not apply. Synthetic scaffolding: head of household (the example says unmarried with a dependent child; household.home_cost Yes); the $6,000 is paid to the institution; the scholarship allocated to tuition does not exceed the period's expenses. The publication's "American opportunity credit" total is the allowed amount: Form 8863 line 8 (refundable) plus line 19 (nonrefundable, limited by the tax). Shown state (from the instructions; T-232): the example allows a $3,325 EIC, so the i1040gi flowchart passes Steps 1 to 3 and reaches Step 5 (each earlier "STOP You can't take the credit" would deny it). Step 5 question 2 (self-employment, clergy, statutory employee) is No for wages only, so Worksheet A is used, not Worksheet B ("Use this worksheet if you answered “Yes” to Step 5, question 2"). Worksheet A line 4: line 3 $29,625 and line 1 $24,125 differ, "No. Go to line 5"; line 5: with one qualifying child, $29,625 is not "less than $23,350", so "No. Look up the amount on line 3" and line 5 is completed.

Stage 14 return: single, wages $10,000, Schedule C loss $2,000. Schedule SE line 4a = line 3 (-$2,000, "If line 3 is more than zero, multiply ... Otherwise, enter amount from line 3"); line 4c "If less than $400, stop; you don't owe self-employment tax", so line 4c is $0 and the person does not file Schedule SE. EIC Worksheet B Part 2 ("Self-Employed NOT Required To File Schedule SE") line 2b -$2,000; line 4b $10,000 - $2,000 = $8,000; AGI $8,000; EIC Table, $8,000, no child: $614.

stage9.eic.two_children.15000 with dependent[c2].kidnapped withheld. Before the fix eic.has_qc was decided true from a lower bound of 1 and Form 1040 line 16 computed. Finding F1 extended to the where-test path: sum_over kept the known entries as a lower bound while another entry's where test awaited dependent.kidnapped, a refusal gate on dependent.lived_half and dependent.eic_child. The unanswered gate can become a refusal, so the counts, the tests decided from them and the return must stay unknown. The withheld child lived with you 4 months and not in the United States for more than half of 2025: the kidnapped answer decides the refusal gates dependent.kidnap_residency and dependent.kidnap_eic only then, so the case keeps an unanswered gate on the where path.

Companion to finding F1: stage9.eic.two_children.15000 with dependent[c2].us_half withheld. That input reaches the where tests only through expressions, not through a refusal gate, so the entry can only add: eic.qc_count is unknown with lower bound 1 and eic.has_qc (eic.qc_count > 0) is still decided true.

stage8.refuse.dependent.married with f1040.status withheld. eic.limit and eic.line5_threshold choose on the filing status first; each status's alternative reads the qualifying-child count, which dependent[child].married refuses (the married child). Whichever status is answered the line is that refusal, so both are refused, not held unknown behind the unanswered status (spec 4.7.3).
